jc.t: Foundation ceremony of the new mandir

w: Swamishri visits the local Jain Mandir for darshan.
Devotees and well-wishers who had contributed and helped in the creation of the new Swaminarayan Mandir were felicitated in a specialy assembly by Swamishri.

2000.o: Swamishri performed arti on inauguration ceremony of Swaminarayan Mandir, Khambhat, Lord Harikrishna Maharaj was honored
w: In the evening, Swamishri arrived in Undel and performed the ground - breaking ceremony for the Swaminarayan Mandir.

At 6.00 p.m., a public Satsang assembly was arranged at the renowned Suntek City Hall in the city center. Many dignitaries welcomed and honored Swamishri. A welcome dance was performed by the local yuvaks. After speeches and bhajans by sadhus, Swamishri addressed the audience of 400 devotees and wellwishers.
Fulfilling the wish of Yogiji Maharaj, the grand new Yogi Assembly Hall was inaugurated by Pramukh Swami Maharaj on Sunday 19 January 2003 at the auspicious time of 10.55 a.m.

Located within the impressive and imposing 10-floor 90,000 sq.ft. Yogi Hall Complex, behind the BAPS Mandir in Dadar, Mumbai, the Yogi Assembly Hall is fully air-conditioned with a seating capacity of around 3500 and is fully equipped with audio-video facilities.

The interior of the hall is beautifully decorated with traditionally sculptured designs in wood. The intricately carved pillars, balconies, windows and the impressive lotus sculptured in the ceiling give the auditorium a traditional spiritual character.
For the women devotees, a two-tier balcony provides ample seating space and a clear view of the 55 x 25 ft.
Below the hall, on the ground floor, is a 1000-capacity multi-purpose auditorium and in the basement is a car park.
In the three floors above the hall are residential facilities for visiting pilgrims and offices for the various local satsang activities.
The complex has been designed and constructed under the supervision of sadhus and satsangis.

The inauguration ceremony was attended by Shri Arun Gujarati, Speaker of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly, Shri Chhagan Bhujbal, Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra and many other dignitaries. Shri Arun Gujarati said, "Only Pramukh Swami can make such a hall. One can see blemishes on the full moon, but there are no blemishes in Pramukh Swami's life. This auditorium, bearing Yogiji Maharaj's name, is probably the first of its kind in India." Chhagan Bhujbal then addressed the assembly, "I have been to Gadhada and also visited Akshardham in Gandhinagar. They are fantastic. Following the Latur earthquake (1993) the Sanstha gave such tremendous help that it can never be forgotten. At such times, Pramukh Swami has not merely remained in the mandirs, but has reached out to the people. One day will come when the whole world will follow Pramukh Swami's path." Blessing the assembly, Swamishri said, "It was the wish of Yogiji Maharaj that a grand assembly hall be built in Mumbai. All his wishes were divine. He also wished that the Narmada Dam project be quickly completed. He always wished for the good of others. It was his wish to build Akshardham in Delhi and land was acquired on the banks of Yamuna. There is great power in his wishes. This project has been completed by the support of the devotees and well-wishers." This special inauguration assembly was attended by over 700 invited guests and devotees. In the evening, over 10,000 devotees attended the first satsang assembly in the new hall.
The sanctified murtis by Swamishri for the hari mandirs in the suburbs of Mira Road and Vasai were installed by Pujya Kothari Swami.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of Shri Akshar-Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Radha-Krishna Dev, Shri Hanumanji and Ganapatji and Guru Parampara for BAPS hari mandir in Dabhan. Thereafter he blessed the devotees.
27 Janruary 2008, (V.S. 2064,r Vad 5) Mumbai Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of murtis for BAPS hari mandirs in Jalundh (Khambhat district) and Vadola.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj was seated on a chair. Tyagratna Swami, who had come from America, spoke of Devvandan Swami's seva and said, "He is actually a chartered accountant, yet in Chicago he does the seva of the garden and maintenance. Whoever comes for darshan is delighted to see the garden. Also, before becoming a sadhu he used to drive a Mercedes, yet he does such seva humbly and with great hard work."
Swamishri said to Devvandan Swami, "This is a great seva you are doing. Even by seeing the garden, everyone feels at peace."

Then he said, "We all have to understand this too. There may be positions and authority, but no ego should come. Whatever seva we get is Thakorji's, so understanding this, we should do it with a sense of its glory. Pride of position should never come. Having become a servant, a sevak, is itself the greatest position, isn't it!"
Tyagratna Swami said, "That is exactly what you have always done, isn't it! We have to follow in your footsteps."

Swamishri said with a smile, "I am here and you are there (in America), so how can you follow in my footsteps?" Then he said, "If we obey the instructions, we can be said to have followed in the footsteps."

ds.t: Being a servant is the greatest post
w: Swamishri was seated on a chair. Tyagratna Swami, who had come from America, spoke of Devvandan Swami's services: "He is actually a chartered accountant, yet in Chicago he does the garden and maintenance seva. Everyone who comes for darshan is very pleased to see the garden. And before becoming a sadhu he drove a Mercedes, yet he does such seva humbly and with great effort."
Swamishri said to Devvandan Swami, "This is great seva you are doing. Even seeing the garden brings everyone peace."

Then he said, "All of us must understand this too. There may be posts and authority, but pride should not come. Whatever seva we get belongs to Thakorji; understand that and do it with a sense of its greatness. Pride of position should never come. Becoming a servant, becoming a sevak, that itself is the great post!"
Tyagratna Swami said, "That is what you have always done! We must walk in your footsteps."
Laughing, Swamishri said, "I am here and you are there (in America), so how can you walk in my footsteps?" Then he said, "If we follow the commands, we are said to walk in the footsteps."

An ambience of a diksha ceremony was set up before Thakorji in the central sanctum of the mandir. Shriji Maharaj was shown engaged in initiating Mulji Bhakta into Gunatitanand Swami. Prior to his puja Swami performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of pujan and arti of murtis for BAPS hari mandirs for suburbs in Mumbai, namely, Kharghar, Kandivali (East) and Virar, and Bodal (Kheda district).

Seated in a Merc, Mahant Swami Maharaj came from Akshar Farm to the mandir. After darshan in the three shrines of the mandir, and darshan of the guru parampara, he came before the murti of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Here his saying had been placed: "Tolerance is the highest dharma."

Then the sadhus, wishing to hear this sentence from Swamishri's lips, began saying sentences that showed a lack of tolerance. Pointing to Pramukh Swami Maharaj's saying, Swamishri said, "Tolerance is the highest dharma."
The sadhus' wish was fulfilled.
Shrijivandandas Swami then asked, "But how long should we tolerate? Is there any limit?"
"No, right up to Akshardham," Swamishri said with a gesture of his hand.
Today the announcement assembly was held for Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 97th birthday celebration to be held in Anand. Mahant Swami Maharaj had given blessings in this assembly
that "Swamibapa's virtues brought liberation, and we will have to acquire them."
After the chesta was over, these blessings Swamishri had given
were recalled one by one by the sadhus.
Atmatruptdas Swami said, "After saying all this, I liked the last thing you said... we just have to pray."
Priyavratdas Swami said, "It is only if we pray that virtues will come."
Swamishri said, "There is no other way."
Priyavratdas Swami said, "You said, 'Virtues yes, but virtues that please God and the Sant,' that was a special point."
Swamishri reinforced it: "Not other virtues."
The sadhus said, "So what do we have to do? Just pray, right?! That you grant us such virtues."
Swamishri said, "Yes, but pray sincerely." Then with emphasis in his tone he said, "Not superficially."
Priyavratdas Swami asked, "But how can one pray sincerely?"
"That comes automatically... one is choked with emotion. One feels it is truly worth praying for. Then that prayer is right," Swamishri said.
Priyavratdas Swami said, "Doctor Swami said, one does not have to pray; it just happens."
Swamishri said "Yes", agreeing.

Atmatruptdas Swami said, "Yogibapa has said, a prayer is one where we do not pray today and go back on it tomorrow. But what happens is, we pray at night before sleeping, 'Wake me early in the morning', but then we feel like sleeping a little more."
Swamishri laughed and burst out, "Bogus prayer."
All the sadhus roared with laughter.
Swamishri went on, "If one has prayed sincerely, one will definitely get up."

Then he said, "There is not much difference between a fake prayer and a real one. Both look true. One sits like this (he made the gesture of praying with folded hands, eyes closed and a choked voice), but it is bogus, completely bogus; the pose is all perfect!"
Atmatruptdas Swami asked, "You can tell whether a prayer is true or false, can't you?"
Swamishri said, "Yes."
Atmatruptdas Swami said, "If it is true, then please do the work."
"At once... instantly," Swamishri said.
Priyavratdas Swami said, "So now we have to pray for that too, that we pray truly."
Everyone laughed.
"But that too will be bogus." Swamishri laid bare our state of mind.
Then he said, "A true prayer has to be made only once."
Priyavratdas Swami asked, "If the prayer is true, is the work done in one go?"
"Yes."
Then Swamishri said, "A series of bogus ones goes on. Bogus, bogus, bogus..."
Everyone felt that such subtle flaws left in our prayers can be caught only by the one who listens to them.
